title: PINN Co-Design Framework
description: A coupled systems map showing why no representation, constraint, numerical, training, or reliability choice has an independent optimum.
represents: PINN development is a coupled scientific-computing formulation. The physical problem and intended role define the demands; representation, physics, numerical realization, and training determine the achievable model; verification closes the system by testing accuracy, trainability, fidelity, cost, and reliability.
interpretation: Changing one domain can alter several others. For example, an architectural change can modify derivative spectra, constraint form, sampling needs, loss conditioning, and optimizer behavior. Evaluation therefore diagnoses coupled design causes rather than ranking components in isolation.

core.title: PINN Co-Design
core.subtitle: Coupled scientific-computing formulation
core.summary: The central formulation coordinates the scientific problem, neural approximation, constraint mechanism, numerical realization, optimization objective, and reliability criteria.

evidence.rationale: The review presents physics-informed learning as a joint design of governing knowledge, data, representation, optimization, and task.
The foundational PINN formulation couples approximation, automatic differentiation, physical residuals, conditions, observations, and inverse quantities in one trainable system.

domains.title: Physical Problem & Computational Role
domains.summary: The governing structure, scales, regularity, geometry, data, and scientific objective set the co-design requirements.

evidence.rationale: Physics-informed method selection is organized around the governing problem, available data, and intended scientific role.
A repeated-query role motivates learning a PDE solution operator instead of fitting a single state.

domains.title: Representation
domains.summary: The ansatz controls state coverage, approximation capacity, inductive bias, regularity, conditioning, and transferability.

evidence.rationale: Fourier features alter multi-scale approximation and spectral behavior, directly supporting representation as a co-design domain.
SIREN representation and adaptive sampling are co-designed for stiff, high-frequency electromagnetic fields.
Latent parameter encoding changes the representation so one PINN can span a parameterized PDE family.

domains.title: Physics & Constraints
domains.summary: Physical content and enforcement mechanisms determine admissibility, constraint coverage, conservation behavior, and residual structure.

evidence.rationale: Exact Dirichlet enforcement changes admissibility and removes a boundary requirement from permanent penalty competition.
Discrete conservative enforcement adds local conservation and interface-flux structure to the physical constraints.
Equality-constrained neural networks treat physical requirements as constraints for forward, inverse, and multi-fidelity problems.

domains.title: Numerical Realization
domains.summary: Differentiation, residual evaluation, sampling, and decomposition determine gradient information, physical coverage, memory, and stability.

evidence.rationale: Coupled automatic–numerical differentiation changes residual accuracy, support coupling, and computation.
Trace estimation redesigns high-order derivative evaluation to reduce memory and runtime.
cv-PINN combines subdomain numerical integration, embedded test functions, and domain decomposition as one numerical realization.
Residual-point placement is shown to change both accuracy and point efficiency across forward and inverse problems.
XPINN realizes spatial and temporal decomposition with local networks, interface conditions, and parallel training.

domains.title: Training & Optimization
domains.summary: The objective and its optimization depend jointly on physics, data, sampling, architecture, scaling, and conditioning.

evidence.rationale: Self-adaptive weighting addresses competition among data, boundary, initial, and PDE objectives.
Gradient-flow pathology analysis links residual stiffness, loss imbalance, architecture, and annealing.
Loss-landscape conditioning is shown to determine whether first-order, hybrid, or second-order optimization succeeds.
Dual-cone descent explicitly treats PDE and boundary losses as a conflicting multi-objective optimization problem.

domains.title: Verification & Reliability
domains.summary: Reliability requires complementary numerical, physical, robustness, uncertainty, identifiability, and efficiency checks.

evidence.rationale: Noisy forward and inverse problems require posterior inference and uncertainty validation, not pointwise fit alone.
Total-uncertainty analysis distinguishes parametric and approximation uncertainty and supports coverage-aware reliability.
Physics-informed variational inference supplies a probabilistic formulation for forward and inverse stochastic equations.
Multi-scale target structure changes which feature spectrum the representation must supply.
Encoding the PDE parameter as a latent representation changes the family of physical states the model can express.
The governing laws and available information determine how physical knowledge enters learning.
High operator order and dimensionality directly change derivative memory and runtime in the coupled formulation.
A boundary-aware trial construction changes whether Dirichlet conditions are exact or optimized as penalties.
Eigenvector bias links PDE-learning behavior to the feature spectrum and representation capacity.
Weak enforcement replaces pointwise residuals with test functions and quadrature, changing the numerical core.
Equality-constrained training changes physical requirements from weighted penalties to explicit constraints.
Conservation-law structure requires discrete subdomains and interface-flux treatment.
Variational constraint form introduces test-function and quadrature decisions.
Residual-point distribution changes the training information and final error across thousands of PINN runs.
High-order residual structure drives derivative memory and runtime.
Coupling AD and ND changes residual stability, sparsity requirements, and computational cost.
Competitive data, condition, and PDE losses define the composite objective and require balancing.

relationships.label: optimizer performance depends on sampling & loss conditioning

evidence.rationale: Differential operators induce loss ill-conditioning that changes optimizer performance.
Residual stiffness produces unbalanced gradients and motivates annealing.
Adaptive activation slopes and slope recovery jointly modify approximation and gradient dynamics.
Noisy inverse problems demonstrate that accuracy and uncertainty must be assessed together.

relationships.label: poor reliability prompts problem or role redesign

evidence.rationale: When repeated-query cost is the failure criterion, the computational role can be redesigned as operator learning.
Poor multi-scale resolution motivates feature-space redesign.
Training pathologies motivate an adaptive activation and slope-recovery response.
Boundary-condition failure motivates exact trial-space enforcement.
Conservation failure motivates a conservative discrete residual and flux continuity.

relationships.label: poor accuracy or conservation prompts resampling / reformulation

evidence.rationale: Observed residual error drives adaptive resampling.
Accuracy and efficiency failures motivate a mixed differentiation pathway.

relationships.label: training diagnostics prompt loss or optimizer redesign

evidence.rationale: Unequal loss progress motivates dynamic reweighting.
Ill-conditioned loss landscapes motivate hybrid or second-order optimization.
